duplicate_therapeutic_classes.reason: Taking multiple NSAIDs concurrently increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding and renal toxicity without added benefit.
Concurrent use of multiple SSRIs increases serotonin syndrome risk without additional antidepressant benefit.
Combining multiple ACE inhibitors provides no additional benefit and increases hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal impairment risk.
Concurrent statin use increases myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk without proportional LDL reduction benefit.
Multiple loop diuretics increase risk of dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, and ototoxicity.
Combining beta-blockers increases bradycardia, hypotension, and heart block risk.
Multiple anticoagulants dramatically increase major bleeding risk without proportional thrombosis prevention benefit.
Multiple antiplatelet agents increase bleeding risk; dual therapy only under specific clinical guidance.
Multiple PPI use increases risk of Clostridium difficile infection, pneumonia, and long-term nutrient deficiencies.
Concurrent anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy requires careful indication review due to additive bleeding risk.
